name: io.github.2016judea/fair-line
title: Fair Line: NFL bet pricing and angle backtests
description: Is this NFL line worth it? Fair prices, officiating edges and real-or-noise trend tests since 1999

tools.name: slate_scan
tools.description: The week's board for every NFL game: consensus spread and total, what each half point is worth when shopping (the price at -4, -3.5, -2.5 that matches the consensus at -110, and how often the game lands on 3 or 7), rest days and travel, a penalty-discipline edge, the National Weather Service forecast for open-air stadiums inside 7 days, and every betting angle that applies to the game, each backtested with its record, win rate and a verdict of holds up, noise, or no edge. Ends with a short ranked list of games worth a look and why. For 'what should I look at this week', 'Thanksgiving games', 'any edges on the slate', 'week 13 board', 'Sunday's games'. Lines are the consensus number and move until kickoff.

week.description: NFL week number, or 'next' (default: the next week with unplayed games).

tools.name: price_line
tools.description: Prices one NFL bet against a fair line: win, push and lose chances, the fair price, expected value per $100, break-even, and a quarter-Kelly stake with the uncertainty haircut, plus what buying or selling half a point is worth (key numbers 3 and 7 priced off real NFL margins, not a bell curve) and teasers. Default fair line is the consensus number; pass your own fair line, total or win probability to price your view. For 'is DAL -3.5 at -110 worth it', 'what are the fair odds on over 47.5', 'should I buy the hook to +3', 'what's KC +3 worth in a 6-point teaser', 'how much should I bet'. Information only: it computes; it never places a bet.

bet.description: The bet in plain words, e.g. 'DAL -3.5 -110', 'over 47.5', 'PHI ML +300', 'KC +3 teaser'. Parsed into the fields below; explicit fields win.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

home.description: Home team, when naming a game.

away.description: Away team, when naming a game.

market.description: Market (default spread; total when side is over/under).

line.description: The side's line, e.g. -3.5 or +7, or the total, e.g. 47.5.

price.description: American price, e.g. -110 or +120 (decimal like 1.91 also works). Default -110.

opponent_price.description: The other side's price, to strip the vig from a moneyline.

fair_line.description: Your own fair spread for this side, if you have one.

fair_win_prob.description: Your win probability for this side, 0-1.

bankroll.description: Bankroll in dollars, to turn the Kelly fraction into a stake.

tools.name: officiating_edge
tools.description: Penalty discipline for both teams (accepted flags against, recent and season-long, shrunk toward the league so a three-game streak doesn't count as a trait), turned into points at 0.8 points a flag, with a 95% interval, and priced against the spread. Add the referee once crews post to see the crew's flag rate. Says plainly what has and hasn't held up: crews do differ in how many flags they throw, but home-crowd whistle and crew home bias measure as noise, and crew flag counts haven't beaten the total. For 'who's reffing and does it matter', 'officiating edge in PHI @ DAL', 'does this crew favor the home team', 'which team gets flagged most'.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

home.description: Home team, when naming a game.

away.description: Away team, when naming a game.

game.description: The game as written, e.g. "PHI at DAL" or "PHI @ DAL" (away team first).

referee.description: Referee's name (last name is enough) once crews are announced, usually midweek.

line.description: Your line for the favoured side, to price the edge (default consensus).

tools.name: backtest_angle
tools.description: Backtests a betting angle or trend on every NFL game since 1999 against the closing number: record, win rate with a 95% interval, the exact chance a coin flip does as well, how it did in the last five seasons held out, season by season, and what the best of 20 random angles looks like at that sample, so a lucky trend is called noise. Filters: team, opponent, home/away, favorite/underdog, line range, total range, off a bye, opponent off a bye, short week, rest edge, division, prime time, weekday, Thanksgiving, week range, playoffs, dome/outdoors, temperature, wind, time zones travelled, miles, after a win/loss/blowout, referee. Bet against the spread, moneyline, over or under. For 'home dogs after a bye, real or noise', 'big road favourites off a loss', 'how do teams do on a short week', 'Thanksgiving road teams ATS'. Pass angles_tried if several angles were looked at, to correct for the search.

bet.description: What to bet (default ats: against the spread).

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

line_min.description: Side's own line at least this (e.g. 3 = dogs of +3 or more; -7 = favourites of 7 or less).

line_max.description: Side's own line at most this.

rest_edge_min.description: At least this many more rest days than the opponent.

after.description: What happened in the team's previous game.

angles_tried.description: How many angles were tried before this one (corrects the p-value for searching).

tools.name: thanksgiving_and_special_games
tools.description: Straight-up, against-the-spread and over/under records for the NFL's special dates since 1999: Thanksgiving (the Lions and Cowboys at home, road teams on a short week, the night game), Black Friday, Christmas Day, international games (London, Germany, Mexico, Brazil, Spain) and the first game back after one, the final regular-season week, and late-season Saturdays. Narrow by team, opponent, home or road, favourite or dog, division, line range or seasons. Answers first with the raw record, n and a 95% interval, then a holds_up block: the last five seasons held out, a false-discovery correction, and an estimate shrunk by how much spots like this actually repeat. Lists the last ten games. For 'Lions on Thanksgiving against the spread', 'how do the Cowboys do on Thanksgiving', 'road teams on Turkey Day ATS', 'Thanksgiving overs', 'Christmas games', 'teams coming back from London', 'Week 18 dogs'.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

line_min.description: Side's own line at least this (e.g. 3 = dogs of +3 or more).

tools.name: player_split
tools.description: How one NFL player does in a spot, and whether it holds up: home vs road, against one opponent, indoors vs outdoors, in the cold (40°F or below), in prime time, division games, vs man or zone coverage and vs the blitz (QBs, since 2023), against his former teams, the game after a bad one, rookie season, and backup QB starts (league-wide when no player is named). Works for QBs (EPA per dropback, passing yards, TDs, picks, completions), running backs (rushing yards, carries, rushing + receiving yards) and receivers and tight ends (receiving yards, receptions, targets, anytime TD). Answers first with the raw split: per-game average on each side, n and a 95% interval, plus career, this-season and recent baselines. Then a holds_up block: how much splits of that kind repeat year to year for NFL players since 2018, how much of his gap survives, and an estimate for his next game in that spot. Give a prop (e.g. 'over 265.5 passing yards -115') to get the hit rate, win chance, fair price and EV. Also returns his team's straight-up, against-the-spread and over/under record in those games. For 'Goff at home vs away', 'Cousins vs the Bears', 'Tua in the cold', 'Allen against the blitz', 'Stafford vs the Lions', 'backup QB starts ATS', 'Lamb receiving yards at home', 'Henry over 89.5 rushing yards', 'player prop', 'QB splits'.

player.description: Player name, e.g. Jared Goff, Goff, CeeDee Lamb. Leave out only for league-wide rookie or backup QB starts.

split.description: Which split (default home_away, or opponent when an opponent is given).

opponent.description: Opponent team for an opponent split, or to narrow any split to games against one team.

venue.description: For home_away: which side to lead with. For other splits: only home or only road games.

metric.description: Stat to split on. Defaults by position: QB EPA per dropback (passing yards when a prop is given), RB rushing yards, WR/TE receiving yards.

prop.description: A prop in plain words, e.g. 'over 265.5 passing yards -115' or 'under 4.5 receptions +105'.

tools.name: team_split
tools.description: One NFL team's straight-up, against-the-spread and over/under record in a spot since 1999: home or road, favourite or underdog, by month (December, January), off a bye, on a short week, after a win or loss or blowout, in prime time, division games, vs one opponent, outdoors in the cold or wind, by line range. Also the lookahead spot (next week is a division game, a prime-time game, or a named rival) and the sandwich spot (a non-division game between two division games). Raw record first with n and a 95% interval, then a holds_up block: the last five seasons held out, a false-discovery correction, and an estimate shrunk by how much team spots repeat. Lists the last ten games. For 'Bills at home in December', 'Packers as road dogs', 'Chiefs after a loss', 'lookahead to Dallas', 'sandwich spot between division games', 'how do the Eagles do on a short week'.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

lookahead.description: Next week's game: 'division', 'prime_time', or a team name (e.g. Cowboys).

sandwich.description: A non-division game with division games the week before and after.

line_min.description: Team's own line at least this (e.g. 3 = dogs of +3 or more).

tools.name: coach_split
tools.description: A head coach's straight-up, against-the-spread and over/under record in a spot, across every team he coached since 1999: off a bye, as a favourite or underdog, home or road, by month, after a loss, in prime time, division games, in the playoffs, and head to head against another coach. Loose names work (Reid, McVay, Harbaugh); a shared last name picks the most recent coach and lists the other. Raw record first with n and a 95% interval, then the holds_up test (held-out seasons, false-discovery correction, shrunk estimate). For 'Reid off a bye', 'Andy Reid after a bye week ATS', 'Harbaugh as an underdog', 'Tomlin as a dog', 'Belichick vs Reid', 'McVay against Shanahan', 'coach vs coach record'.

coach.description: Head coach, e.g. Andy Reid, Reid, Sean McVay.

opponent_coach.description: Opposing head coach, for coach vs coach.

tools.name: head_to_head
tools.description: Two NFL teams' head-to-head series since 1999: who leads it, the last ten meetings, straight up, against the spread and over/under, home or road, in the rematch. Without two teams it answers the rivalry spots: division underdogs, dogs in a same-season rematch. Raw record first with n and a 95% interval, then the holds_up test (held-out seasons, false-discovery correction, shrunk estimate). Lists the last ten meetings. For 'do the Packers own the Bears', 'Cowboys Eagles head to head last 10', 'who owns who', 'division rivalry dogs', 'dogs in the rematch', 'Ravens vs Steelers series ATS'.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

last_n.description: Only the last N meetings, e.g. 10.

rematch.description: Second (or later) meeting of the same regular season.

tools.name: revenge_game
tools.description: Do revenge spots cover? Three kinds, since 1999: the rematch (a team that lost the earlier meeting that season, optionally by a set margin), a starting quarterback facing a team he used to start for, and a head coach facing a team he used to coach. Name a team, a QB or a coach to narrow it; add home or road, favourite or dog. Raw record first with n and a 95% interval, then the holds_up test (held-out seasons, false-discovery correction, shrunk estimate), and the last ten games. For 'revenge game', 'revenge spot after losing the first meeting', 'facing his old team', 'Baker vs his old team', 'Stafford vs the Lions', 'coach against his former team'.

kind.description: Which revenge spot (default rematch; qb or coach when one is named).

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.

qb.description: Starting quarterback, e.g. Baker Mayfield, Stafford.

lost_first_meeting_by.description: Rematch only: lost the earlier meeting by at least this many points.

tools.name: primetime_and_weather_spots
tools.description: Straight-up, against-the-spread and over/under records since 1999 for prime-time and weather spots: Thursday, Sunday and Monday night, any prime-time kickoff, outdoor games at 40°F or colder, 32°F or colder (snow isn't recorded; this stands in for it), 15+ mph wind, 85°F+ heat, dome teams on the road outdoors or in the cold, and warm-weather teams in the cold. Narrow by team, opponent, home or road, favourite or dog, division, seasons. Raw record first with n and a 95% interval, then the holds_up test (held-out seasons, false-discovery correction, shrunk estimate), and the last ten games. For 'TNF unders', 'SNF favourites', 'MNF home dogs', 'Dolphins under 40 degrees', 'dome teams in the cold', 'wind over 15 unders', 'do unders hit in wind', 'snow games', 'warm-weather teams in December cold'.

team.description: Team: abbreviation, city or nickname, e.g. DAL, Dallas, Cowboys.
